\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{در} \fa{آن} \fa{زمان} (dar ân zamân)}{در آن زمان (dar ân zamân)}]{\fa{در} \fa{آن} \fa{زمان} (dar ân zamân) — at that time, back then}

\label{lesson:FA-C304-dar-an-zaman}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for at the very end, then the Persian for ultimately.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{در} \fa{آن} \fa{زمان}}
\textbf{\fa{در} \fa{آن} \fa{زمان}} (\emph{dar ân zamân}) — \textquotedblleft{}at that time, back then\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{در} \fa{آن} \fa{زمان} \fa{ما} \fa{در} \fa{یک} \fa{روستا} \fa{زندگی} \fa{میکردیم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Dar ân zamân mâ dar yek rustâ zendegi mikardim.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
At that time we lived in a village.
\end{quote}

It sets the scene, so the verb is often the past continuous: \emph{zendegi mikardim}. In speech \emph{un moqe'}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{dar} \textquotedblleft{}in\textquotedblright{} and \emph{ân} \textquotedblleft{}that\textquotedblright{} are inherited Persian. \emph{zamân} \textquotedblleft{}time\textquotedblright{} is found in Middle Persian and in Arabic alike; EtymDB lists it with no parent, and its origin is not settled.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dar ân zamân}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{dar ân zamân}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for at the very end, then the Persian for ultimately, then say \emph{dar ân zamân} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{قدیم} (qadim)}{قدیم (qadim)}]{\fa{قدیم} (qadim) — the old days, olden times}

\label{lesson:FA-C304-qadim}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for ultimately, then the Persian for at that time.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{قدیم}}
\textbf{\fa{قدیم}} (\emph{qadim}) — \textquotedblleft{}the old days, olden times\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{در} \fa{قدیم} \fa{مردم} \fa{با} \fa{اسب} \fa{سفر} \fa{میکردند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Dar qadim mardom bâ asb safar mikardand.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
In the old days people travelled on horseback.
\end{quote}

\emph{Qadim-hâ} \textquotedblleft{}long ago\textquotedblright{} in speech. The adjective for old things is \emph{qadimi}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{qadim} is borrowed from Arabic \emph{qadīm}, \textquotedblleft{}old, ancient\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{بعدها} (ba'dhâ)}{بعدها (ba'dhâ)}]{\fa{بعدها} (ba'dhâ) — later on, afterwards}

\label{lesson:FA-C304-badha}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for at that time, then the Persian for the old days.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{بعدها}}
\textbf{\fa{بعدها}} (\emph{ba'dhâ}) — \textquotedblleft{}later on, afterwards\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{بعدها} \fa{فهمیدم} \fa{که} \fa{او} \fa{راست} \fa{میگفت}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Ba'dhâ fahmidam ke u râst migoft.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Later on I realised that he had been telling the truth.
\end{quote}

It looks forward from a point in the story, often by years. Built on \emph{ba'd} \textquotedblleft{}after\textquotedblright{} with the plural \emph{-hâ}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{ba'dhâ} adds the Persian plural ending \emph{-hâ} to \emph{ba'd} \textquotedblleft{}after\textquotedblright{}, which is borrowed from Arabic \emph{ba'd} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for at that time, then the Persian for the old days, then say \emph{ba'dhâ} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{از} \fa{آن} \fa{پس} (az ân pas)}{از آن پس (az ân pas)}]{\fa{از} \fa{آن} \fa{پس} (az ân pas) — from then on, after that}

\label{lesson:FA-C304-az-an-pas}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for the old days, then the Persian for later on.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{از} \fa{آن} \fa{پس}}
\textbf{\fa{از} \fa{آن} \fa{پس}} (\emph{az ân pas}) — \textquotedblleft{}from then on, after that\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{از} \fa{آن} \fa{پس} \fa{هر} \fa{روز} \fa{ورزش} \fa{میکرد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Az ân pas har ruz varzesh mikard.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
From then on he exercised every day.
\end{quote}

Formal; in speech \emph{az un be ba'd}. With the past continuous it describes a new habit.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{az} \textquotedblleft{}from\textquotedblright{}, \emph{ân} \textquotedblleft{}that\textquotedblright{} and \emph{pas} \textquotedblleft{}after\textquotedblright{} are all inherited Persian; \emph{pas} continues Middle Persian \emph{pas}, \textquotedblleft{}then, afterwards, behind\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{اخیرا} (akhiran)}{اخیرا (akhiran)}]{\fa{اخیرا} (akhiran) — recently, lately}

\label{lesson:FA-C304-akhiran}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for later on, then the Persian for from then on.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{اخیرا}}
\textbf{\fa{اخیرا}} (\emph{akhiran}) — \textquotedblleft{}recently, lately\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{اخیرا} \fa{یک} \fa{کتاب} \fa{جدید} \fa{خریدم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Akhiran yek ketâb-e jadid kharidam.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I recently bought a new book.
\end{quote}

Formal; in speech \emph{tâzegi-hâ}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{akhiran} is usually traced to Arabic \emph{akhīran}, \textquotedblleft{}lately\textquotedblright{}, the adverb of \emph{akhīr} \textquotedblleft{}last\textquotedblright{} with the ending \emph{-an}; EtymDB lists no entry for it.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
